newsitem.title: USA: Disney posts higher profits on growth in all units.
newsitem.headline: Disney posts higher profits on growth in all units.

text.p: Walt Disney Co. Tuesday reported higher fourth-quarter operating profits and revenues, reflecting improved results in all three of its major divisions -- broadcasting, creative content and theme parks and resorts.
The pro forma results assume that Capital Cities/ABC Inc. was part of Disney during all of both the most recent and the year-ago period. Capital Cities/ABC was acquired by Disney last February.

The giant entertainment company said operating income for the three months ended Sept. 30 rose 27 percent to $858 million. Net income rose 60 percent to $354 million and revenues rose 12 percent to $5.3 billion.
Revenues for the fiscal year increased 12 percent to $21.2 billion and operating income increased 7 percent to $3.7 billion.
Net income for the fiscal year increased 16 percent to $1.5 billion, and earnings per share increased 15 percent to $2.23.

The quarter and fiscal year pro forma data reflect a full period of operating results for both Walt Disney Co. and ABC, and a full period impact of amortization of intangible assets, interest expense, the new effective income tax rate and additional shares outstanding related to the acquisition.

"I am extremely pleased with the progress we have made in integrating Disney and ABC," Disney Chairman and Chief Executive Michael Eisner said in a statement. "The fact that we continued our strong growth during this period proves that the combined operations are working and working well."
Disney said theme parks set attendance records for the year, with revenues for the quarter rising 11 percent to $1.2 billion and operating income up 16 percent to $242 million.
For the fiscal year, theme parks revenues increased 13 percent to $4.5 billion and operating income rose 15 percent to $990 million.

Disney said the quarterly results at the theme parks and resorts unit reflected record attendance, exceeding the record levels achieved in the prior year, and increased guest spending at Walt Disney World and Disneyland.

Creative Content, which includes Disney's core motion picture studio operations, reported pro forma revenues for the quarter up 18 percent to $2.7 billion and operating income up 31 percent to $387 million.
For the fiscal year, the unit's revenues increased 17 percent to $10.5 billion while operating income of $1.6 billion was about equal to the prior-year performance.

Disney said Creative Content results for the quarter reflected the domestic home video releases of "Oliver & Company" and "Aladdin and the King of Thieves," the domestic box office success of "Phenomenon" and strong international theatrical performances by "The Rock" and "The Hunchback of Notre Dame."
Results for the quarter also reflected growth in international consumer products licensing.

The fiscal year results reflected the domestic home video success of "Cinderella," "Pocahontas" and "The Aristocats," the global home video performances of "The Lion King" and "101 Dalmatians," and world growth in consumer products licensing.

Results for the year also reflected the successful performance of various live-action titles in the home video and pay TV markets, including "The Santa Clause," "While You Were Sleeping" and "Crimson Tide," as well as the worldwide theatrical success of "Toy Story."
Disney said the results were offset by lower domestic theatrical film performances, the write-off of certain projects during the second quarter, and difficult comparisons to the prior-year period.
Broadcasting pro forma revenues increased 4 percent to $1.4 billion for the quarter and operating income increased 36 percent to $229 million.
For the year, revenues increased 4 percent to $6.2 billion and operating income increased 12 percent to $1.1 billion.
Disney said broadcasting results for both periods benefited from significant reductions in programme amortization and other costs attributable to the ABC acquisition.
The year results also reflect increases in advertising and affiliate revenues at ESPN, the cable sports network.

On an as-reported basis, reflecting Capital City/ABC's results from the effective date of the acquisition on Feb. 9, Disney's revenues for the quarter increased 69 percent to $5.3 billion and operating income rose 73 percent to $858 million.
Net income increased 27 percent to $336 million and earnings per share decreased 2 percent to 49 cents a share.
For the fiscal year, revenues increased 54 percent to $18.7 billion, but net income fell to $1.21 billion from $1.38 billion.

The 1996 results included two non-recurring charges during the second quarter -- a $300 million non-cash charge related to the implementation of an accounting change and a $225 million charge for costs related to the ABC acquisition.
Without the charge, net income rose to $1.53 billion from $1.38 billion.
Disney's stock climbed $1.25 to $74.75 in early trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
